0: My Hero Academia by Kohei Horikoshi (Viz Media) is a big-hearted superhero action story. In a world where most people are born with a superpower called a Quirk, Izuku Midoriya is one of the few born without one, but he still dreams of becoming a hero. Then a chance meeting with All Might, the greatest hero of all, changes everything. It's full of school rivalries, training arcs and big battles, and it's a great pick for fans of classic shonen.
1: One-Punch Man by ONE and Yusuke Murata (Viz Media) is a superhero action comedy. Saitama trained so hard that he can now defeat any enemy with a single punch, and that's exactly his problem. Bored by fights that never challenge him, he joins the Hero Association, hoping to find an opponent worth the effort. Murata's detailed, explosive art pairs with deadpan humor, so it works for action fans and anyone who enjoys a good superhero parody.
2: Komi Can't Communicate by Tomohito Oda (Viz Media) is a gentle, funny school comedy. Shoko Komi is the most admired girl at her high school, but everyone mistakes her silence for elegance. Only her seatmate, Hitohito Tadano, realizes she has a crippling communication disorder and badly wants friends, so he decides to help her make 100 of them. The short chapters are sweet and quirky, perfect for anyone who likes cozy slice-of-life humor.
3: Jujutsu Kaisen by Gege Akutami (Viz Media) is a dark, fast-paced supernatural action series. High schooler Yuji Itadori has amazing physical strength but no interest in the occult, until a cursed object turns up at his school. To save his friends, he swallows a finger of the powerful curse Ryomen Sukuna, ends up sharing his body with it, and lands at Jujutsu High training to fight curses. It's a great fit for readers who like stylish fights and real stakes.
4: Naruto by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a classic ninja adventure. Naruto Uzumaki is a loud, lonely troublemaker in the Hidden Leaf Village, shunned for the fox spirit sealed inside him, who dreams of becoming Hokage and proving everyone wrong. Placed on a team with the brilliant Sasuke and the clever Sakura, he starts taking on real missions. It's a story about friendship, rivalry and hard work that has hooked readers for two decades.
5: A Certain Magical Index by Kazuma Kamachi (Yen Press) is a science-meets-magic action series. Touma Kamijou is an unlucky student in Academy City, a city built around training psychic powers, and his right hand can cancel out any supernatural ability. One day he finds a young nun named Index hanging over his balcony, and she has memorized 103,000 forbidden grimoires that magicians will do anything to get. Fans of big, sprawling worlds will find a lot to dig into.
6: Golden Kamuy by Satoru Noda (Viz Media) is a historical adventure set in early 1900s Hokkaido. Saichi Sugimoto, a Russo-Japanese War veteran known as "Immortal Sugimoto," is panning for gold when he hears of a hidden fortune in Ainu gold whose map is tattooed on the bodies of escaped convicts. He teams up with Asirpa, a young Ainu hunter, to find it. It mixes survival, violence, humor and rich detail about Ainu culture and food.
7: Ai Yori Aoshi by Kou Fumizuki (Tokyopop) is a sweet, old-fashioned romantic comedy. Kaoru Hanabishi is a college student who walked away from his wealthy, overbearing family. One day Aoi Sakuraba, a young woman in a kimono who was promised to him as a child and has loved him ever since, arrives in Tokyo looking for him, and the two end up secretly living together. It's a gentle, warm read for fans of classic romance.
8: Blue Exorcist by Kazue Kato (Viz Media) is a supernatural action series. Rin Okumura is a hot-tempered teenager raised by a priest, until he learns that he's actually the son of Satan. After tragedy strikes, he vows to fight back and enrolls at True Cross Academy to train as an exorcist alongside his twin brother, Yukio. It's a fun mix of school life, demon battles and family drama, with great character designs.
9: Fairy Tail by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a bright, energetic fantasy adventure. Lucy Heartfilia is a young celestial wizard who dreams of joining Fairy Tail, the most famous and rowdy wizards' guild in the kingdom. When she meets Natsu Dragneel, a fire-eating wizard searching for the dragon who raised him, he brings her into the guild, and their jobs turn into one adventure after another. It's all about friendship, magic battles and found family.
10: Oshi no Ko by Aka Akasaka (Yen Press) is a gripping drama about the dark side of show business. Gorou is a small-town doctor and a devoted fan of the teen idol Ai Hoshino, until a strange twist of fate has him reborn as one of her secret twin children. As the twins grow up in the entertainment world, a tragedy sets them on very different paths. It's part mystery and part sharp look at idols, acting and online fame.
12: Rurouni Kenshin by Nobuhiro Watsuki (Viz Media) is a samurai action story set in Meiji-era Japan. Himura Kenshin was once the legendary assassin Battosai, but he now wanders the country with a reverse-blade sword, having vowed never to kill again. When he meets Kaoru Kamiya, who runs a struggling sword school in Tokyo, he finds a place to stay, though his past keeps catching up with him. It's a classic with great sword fights and a lot of heart.
15: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? On the Side: Sword Oratoria by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy action spin-off. It follows Aiz Wallenstein, the famous "Sword Princess" of the Loki Familia and one of the strongest adventurers in the city of Orario. While Bell Cranel's story plays out in the main series, Aiz and her familia take on expeditions of their own deep in the Dungeon. Fans of the main series will enjoy seeing its world from the other side.
16: Rent-a-Girlfriend by Reiji Miyajima (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy full of awkward situations. After his girlfriend dumps him, college student Kazuya Kinoshita uses an app to rent a date. His rental girlfriend, Chizuru Mizuhara, seems perfect, until he finds out she's also his classmate and next-door neighbor, and when their families get the wrong idea, the two are stuck keeping up the act. It's a good pick for readers who enjoy messy, cringe-funny romance.
17: Love Hina by Ken Akamatsu (Tokyopop) is a classic harem romantic comedy. Keitaro Urashima has failed the Tokyo University entrance exam twice, but he's still determined to keep a childhood promise to a girl he can barely remember. When he goes to stay at his grandmother's inn, he discovers it's now an all-girls dormitory, and he's suddenly its new manager. It's a lively, slapstick-heavy romance that helped shape the genre.
18: Children of the Whales by Abi Umeda (Viz Media) is a beautiful, melancholy fantasy. Chakuro is the young archivist of the Mud Whale, a drifting island on an endless sea of sand whose people have magical powers but are fated to die young. When the islanders find a mysterious girl named Lykos on a wrecked island, their quiet world is upended. It's a moving story with lovely art, for readers who enjoy thoughtful, bittersweet fantasy.
19: Frieren: Beyond Journey's End by Kanehito Yamada (Viz Media) is a quiet, thoughtful fantasy adventure. The elf mage Frieren helped a party of heroes defeat the Demon King, but for her, their ten-year journey passed in the blink of an eye. When her old friend Himmel passes away decades later, she realizes she never really got to know him and sets out on a new journey to understand people. It's gentle, funny and often moving.
20: One Piece by Eiichiro Oda (Viz Media) is a sweeping pirate adventure. Monkey D. Luffy ate a mysterious Devil Fruit as a boy and now has a body made of rubber. He sets out to sea to find the legendary treasure called One Piece and become King of the Pirates, gathering a crew of misfits who become family along the way. It's funny, heartfelt and packed with imaginative islands, perfect for anyone who loves a long adventure.
21: My Dress-Up Darling by Shinichi Fukuda (Square Enix) is a sweet, funny romantic comedy about cosplay. Wakana Gojo is a shy high schooler who dreams of crafting traditional hina dolls and keeps his hobby a secret. When the popular Marin Kitagawa finds him at the sewing machine, she asks him to make her a cosplay costume, and their teamwork soon grows into something more. It's warm and full of craft details, great for fans of slow-burn romance.
22: Rin-ne by Rumiko Takahashi (Viz Media) is a lighthearted supernatural comedy. Ever since she vanished as a little girl, Sakura Mamiya has been able to see ghosts. In high school she discovers that the boy next to her, Rinne Rokudo, is a completely broke part-shinigami who guides lost spirits, and she soon gets pulled into his ghost-hunting jobs. It's a fun, episodic read, great for fans of Takahashi's earlier comedies.
24: Attack on Titan by Hajime Isayama (Kodansha) is an intense dark fantasy. Humanity lives behind enormous walls to hide from Titans, giants that devour people. When a colossal Titan breaks through, young Eren Yeager watches his home fall, swears to wipe out every Titan, and joins the military with his friends Mikasa and Armin. Full of shocking twists and big questions about freedom and war, it's for readers who like gripping, mature stories.
25: Boruto: Naruto Next Generations by Ukyo Kodachi and Mikio Ikemoto (Viz Media) is a ninja action series that continues the story of Naruto. Boruto Uzumaki is the son of Naruto, now the Seventh Hokage, and he resents living in the shadow of a father who's too busy to spend time with him. As Boruto heads into the Chunin Exams with his own team, he must figure out what kind of ninja he wants to be. Naruto fans will enjoy the new generation.
26: The Quintessential Quintuplets by Negi Haruba (Kodansha) is a romantic comedy with a mystery at its heart. Futaro Uesugi is a poor but brilliant high schooler who takes a high-paying tutoring job to help his family. His new students turn out to be the wealthy Nakano quintuplets, who hate studying and want nothing to do with him, and from the start we know he'll marry one of them, but which one? It's fun for anyone who likes guessing games and romance.
27: A.I. Love You by Ken Akamatsu (Tokyopop) is an early romantic comedy from the creator of Love Hina. Hitoshi Kobe is a high school student who's hopeless at everything except programming, and he spends his time building artificial intelligence programs. One day a strange accident brings one of them, a cheerful girl named Saati, out of the computer and into the real world. It's sweet, silly and very much of its era, great for fans of classic manga.
28: Dears by Peach-Pit (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi romantic comedy. When a spaceship full of friendly aliens called Dears lands in Japan, the visitors are allowed to live among humans. High schooler Takeya Ikuhara wants nothing to do with them, until he rescues a Dear named Ren, who decides he is her master and leaves him to keep her out of trouble. It's a light, playful read from the creators of Rozen Maiden.
29: Dragon Ball Super by Akira Toriyama (Viz Media) is an action adventure that picks up after the defeat of Majin Buu. Goku is enjoying peaceful life on Earth when Beerus, the God of Destruction, wakes from a long sleep looking for a worthy opponent. That challenge opens the door to gods, other universes and stronger fighters than Goku has ever faced. It's full of big battles and the classic Dragon Ball humor, perfect for longtime fans.
30: The Promised Neverland by Kaiu Shirai (Viz Media) is a tense, clever thriller. Emma, Norman and Ray are the smartest children at Grace Field House, a loving orphanage they've never been allowed to leave. One night they discover the horrifying truth about what happens to the children who are adopted, and they start planning an escape. It's a smart, suspenseful read for anyone who loves mind games and big reveals.
31: Silver Spoon by Hiromu Arakawa (Yen Press) is a warm, funny slice-of-life story from the creator of Fullmetal Alchemist. Burned out by pressure to succeed, city kid Yugo Hachiken enrolls at an agricultural high school in rural Hokkaido, expecting an easy ride. Instead, he faces early mornings, farm chores and classmates who already know their futures. It's down to earth and full of heart, for readers who enjoy coming-of-age stories.
32: As Miss Beelzebub Likes by Matoba (Yen Press) is a cute, gentle comedy set in Hell. Beelzebub is one of the most powerful rulers of the underworld, adored by everyone and secretly obsessed with soft, fluffy things. Her devoted new aide, Mullin, can barely handle how cute she is, and their workplace slowly turns into a sweet romance. It's a cozy read with lots of fun demon characters, great for fans of light comedy.
33: The Saga of Tanya the Evil by Chika Tojo (Yen Press) is a dark military fantasy. A ruthless salaryman is killed and sent by a being calling itself God to be reborn as a little girl in a war-torn world. Now Tanya Degurechaff, she becomes a mage in the Empire's army, determined to survive and rise through the ranks. It's darkly funny and packed with battles and strategy, for readers who like morally gray leads.
34: Don't Toy with Me, Miss Nagatoro by Nanashi (Vertical) is a teasing romantic comedy. Naoto Hachioji is a shy upperclassman who spends his free time drawing alone in the art club room. When younger student Hayase Nagatoro stumbles across his manga, she starts teasing him mercilessly and keeps coming back, and little by little both of them start to change. It's a fun, slow-burn romance for fans of high school comedies.
35: Mission: Yozakura Family by Hitsuji Gondaira (Viz Media) is an action comedy about a family of spies. Taiyo Asano is a shy teen whose only friend is his childhood friend Mutsumi Yozakura, heir to a family of super spies whose overprotective brothers want any guy near her gone. To stay alive, Taiyo marries her and joins the family business. It's a fun mix of action, family chaos and sweet romance.
37: Rainbow Days by Minami Mizuno (Viz Media) is a lighthearted romantic comedy about four high school boys. Natsuki Hashiba is a sweet, hopeless romantic who falls for a girl named Anna after a chance meeting on Christmas Eve. His three best friends, a playboy, an otaku and a quiet sadist, each have their own ideas about how he should win her over. It's a funny, warm look at friendship and first love from the boys' side.
38: Black Butler by Yana Toboso (Yen Press) is a gothic mystery set in Victorian England. Ciel Phantomhive is a young earl who serves as the Queen's "watchdog," handling London's darkest cases. His butler, Sebastian, can do absolutely anything, because he's a demon bound to Ciel by a contract, and together they take on murders, secret societies and the supernatural. It's stylish, darkly funny and great for fans of gothic drama.
39: Black Clover by Yuki Tabata (Viz Media) is a high-energy fantasy action series. In a kingdom where everyone can use magic, Asta is the one boy born without any, and he and his gifted rival, Yuno, both dream of becoming the Wizard King. When Asta receives a mysterious five-leaf grimoire that lets him cancel magic, he joins the Black Bulls, the rowdiest squad of Magic Knights. It's a fun pick for readers who love underdogs and big battles.
40: How Not to Summon a Demon Lord by Yukiya Murasaki (Seven Seas) is a fantasy comedy for mature readers. Takuma Sakamoto is a gamer known online as the demon lord Diablo. When he's summoned into a world just like his favorite game, the two girls who called him try to bind him as their servant, the spell backfires, and he's stuck acting like a powerful demon lord. It's a fan-service-heavy isekai with plenty of humor.
42: Twin Star Exorcists by Yoshiaki Sukeno (Viz Media) is a supernatural action romance. Rokuro Enmado was once a gifted exorcist, but after a tragedy he swore off fighting the monsters called Kegare. Then he meets Benio Adashino, a stubborn girl exorcist, and learns the two of them are prophesied to be the Twin Star Exorcists, a couple whose child will be the strongest exorcist of all. It's a fun mix of battles, bickering and romance.
43: Cirque du Freak by Darren Shan (Yen Press) is a creepy horror adventure. Darren and his best friend Steve sneak into a mysterious freak show that has come to town, where Darren sees a vampire, Mr. Crepsley, and an amazing performing spider he can't stop thinking about. One reckless choice later, his ordinary life is gone for good. This manga version of the popular novels is dark and fast-paced, great for readers who like horror with a coming-of-age story.
44: The Ancient Magus Bride by Kore Yamazaki (Seven Seas) is a gentle, dark fantasy. Chise Hatori is a lonely teenager with no family and no hope, so she sells herself at an auction. She's bought by Elias Ainsworth, a mysterious mage with a skull for a head, who makes her his apprentice and someday his bride, and in his English countryside home she discovers a world of magic and fairies. It's beautiful, thoughtful and quietly emotional.
45: Is It Wrong to Try to Pick Up Girls in a Dungeon? by Fujino Omori (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure. Bell Cranel is a rookie adventurer in Orario, a city built over a huge Dungeon, and the only member of the goddess Hestia's familia. When the famous swordswoman Aiz Wallenstein saves him from a monster, he falls for her instantly and decides to get stronger. It's a fun, upbeat dungeon crawler with a lot of heart.
46: Chronicles of an Aristocrat Reborn in Another World by Yashu (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy adventure. After an untimely death, a young man is reborn in a world of magic as Cain von Silford, the third son of a noble family. The delighted gods shower him with blessings, and he quickly grows ridiculously powerful, which he now has to keep secret. It's an easygoing isekai for readers who enjoy overpowered heroes and cheerful fun.
47: Bleach by Tite Kubo (Viz Media) is a stylish supernatural action series. Ichigo Kurosaki is a teenager who can see ghosts, which has never been more than a nuisance, until he meets Rukia Kuchiki, a Soul Reaper who protects the living from evil spirits called Hollows. When she's injured protecting his family, she gives him her powers, and Ichigo becomes a Soul Reaper himself. It's known for its cool designs, sword fights and huge cast.
49: Jing: King of Bandits by Yuichi Kumakura (Tokyopop) is a whimsical fantasy adventure. Jing is a young thief so skilled that people call him the King of Bandits. With his wisecracking albatross partner, Kir, he travels from one strange, dreamlike city to the next, pulling off mostly self-contained heists of treasures no one else could steal. It's playful and stylish, great for readers who like episodic adventure.
50: Goblin Slayer by Kumo Kagyu (Yen Press) is a gritty dark fantasy for mature readers. A young Priestess joins her very first adventuring party, but their simple goblin hunt goes horribly wrong. She's saved by a mysterious armored warrior known only as Goblin Slayer, who hunts goblins and nothing else, and she decides to join him. It's violent and intense, best for readers who want a harsher take on the adventurer fantasy.
51: Made in Abyss by Akihito Tsukushi (Seven Seas) is a dark fantasy adventure. Riko is an orphan training to be a Cave Raider in a town built around the Abyss, a giant chasm full of strange creatures and relics, and she dreams of following her legendary mother to its depths. After she finds Reg, a robot boy who looks human, a message from her mother arrives and the two set out to descend. Its cute art hides an intense, sometimes disturbing story for older readers.
52: The Seven Deadly Sins: Four Knights of the Apocalypse by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure sequel to The Seven Deadly Sins. Percival is a cheerful boy who has spent his whole life on a remote mountain with his grandfather. When a knight turns his world upside down, he leaves home for the first time and learns of a prophecy about four knights destined to destroy the world. It's full of action and fun new characters.
53: Tokyo Babylon by CLAMP (Yen Press) is a supernatural drama set in 1990s Tokyo. Subaru Sumeragi is a gentle teenage onmyoji, the head of a powerful clan of spiritual mediums, who takes on cases of curses and restless spirits. He's joined by his outgoing twin sister, Hokuto, and Seishiro, a kind veterinarian who claims he's in love with Subaru. It's moody and stylish, and this CLAMP Premium Collection edition is a great way to read it.
55: Blue Lock by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Yusuke Nomura (Kodansha) is an intense soccer drama. After Japan's loss at the World Cup, the soccer union launches Blue Lock, a training program that brings together 300 young strikers. Yoichi Isagi is one of the players invited, and only one of them will become the country's ace striker while the rest will never play for Japan again. It's a high-stakes sports story with big egos, perfect for readers who love fierce competition.
57: Deadman Wonderland by Jinsei Kataoka and Kazuma Kondou (Viz Media) is a violent horror action series. Ganta Igarashi is an ordinary middle schooler until a mysterious figure called the Red Man massacres his whole class. Framed for the killings, Ganta is sentenced to death at Deadman Wonderland, a prison run as an amusement park where inmates fight for their lives. It's dark, fast and bloody, best for older readers who like intense survival stories.
58: Elemental Gelade by Mayumi Azuma (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure. Coud Van Giruet is a young sky pirate who finds a girl named Ren sleeping inside a crate of stolen cargo. Ren is an Edel Raid, a living weapon who can fuse with a human partner, and since plenty of people want her, Coud promises to get her where she wants to go. It's a fun, fast-moving adventure with lively characters, though the English release didn't finish the series.
59: Love Me, Love Me Not by Io Sakisaka (Viz Media) is a sweet shojo romance about friends who see love differently. Yuna is a shy, romantic dreamer waiting for her prince, while Akari, her new neighbor, is a practical realist, and the two become best friends anyway. When Akari's stepbrother Rio and his friend Kazuomi come into the picture, their friendship is tested. It's heartfelt and relatable.
60: Accomplishments of the Duke's Daughter by Reia (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance with a smart lead. Iris is a duke's daughter who suddenly realizes she's been reborn as the villainess of a romance game, at the exact moment her prince fiancé breaks off their engagement. Sent away in disgrace to her family's lands, she uses modern knowledge to turn the struggling territory around. It's satisfying and clever, for readers who like capable heroines.
61: The Seven Deadly Sins by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) is a fantasy action adventure. The Seven Deadly Sins were once the kingdom's greatest knights, until they were framed for treason and scattered. Years later, Princess Elizabeth goes looking for them to save her kingdom and finds Meliodas, the Sins' former leader, running a traveling tavern with his talking pig, Hawk. It's full of battles, humor and heart.
62: Fruits Basket by Natsuki Takaya (Tokyopop) is a beloved shojo story about family and healing. Tohru Honda is a cheerful orphan living in a tent, until the mysterious Sohma family takes her in. She soon learns their secret: several of them turn into animals of the Chinese zodiac when hugged by the opposite sex, and the curse brings them real pain. It's funny, touching and an all-time classic.
63: My Youth Romantic Comedy Is Wrong, As I Expected by Wataru Watari (Yen Press) is a sharp, funny high school comedy. Hachiman Hikigaya is a cynical loner who thinks the whole idea of a happy school life is a lie. After he turns in an essay mocking youth, his teacher forces him to join the Service Club with the brilliant, icy Yukino Yukinoshita, helping other students with their problems. It's witty and surprisingly thoughtful about friendship.
64: Go! Go! Loser Ranger! by Negi Haruba (Kodansha) is a darkly funny action series. Every week, the beloved hero team known as the Dragon Keepers defeats the Dusters, an evil army that is really just putting on a show. Fighter D, one of the Dusters' lowest grunts, is sick of losing on purpose and sets out to take down the heroes himself. It's a fun twist on the Super Sentai formula, great for readers who like underdogs and clever action.
65: Sekirei by Sakurako Gokurakuin (Yen Press) is a fan-service-heavy action comedy for mature readers. Minato Sahashi has failed his college entrance exams twice and is down on his luck. Then a girl named Musubi literally falls from the sky into his life, and she's a Sekirei, one of 108 superpowered beings who must find human partners and battle each other in a mysterious game. It's a lively mix of fights, romance and comedy.
67: The Remarried Empress by Alphatart (Ize Press) is a romantic fantasy drama. Navier is the perfect empress of the Eastern Empire, admired by everyone except, it seems, her husband. When Emperor Sovieshu openly favors a runaway slave named Rashta and finally asks for a divorce, Navier accepts on one condition: she'll remarry, this time to Heinrey, prince of the Western Kingdom. It's elegant and dramatic, for fans of court intrigue.
68: My Hero Academia: Vigilantes by Hideyuki Furuhashi (Viz Media) is a superhero spin-off of My Hero Academia. Koichi Haimawari is a college student with a weak Quirk who never made it into hero school, but he still helps people around town, which is technically illegal without a license. When he teams up with an aspiring idol and a mysterious veteran vigilante, he gets drawn into the city's underground. Fans of the main series will love it.
69: Magi by Shinobu Ohtaka (Viz Media) is a fantasy adventure inspired by the Arabian Nights. Aladdin is a cheerful young boy traveling with a flute that holds Ugo, a powerful djinn. When he meets Alibaba, a young man dreaming of riches, the two team up to conquer one of the mysterious dungeons that have appeared all over the world. It grows from fun adventure into a big story about kingdoms and fate, for readers who love world-building.
70: Kemono Jihen by Sho Aimoto (Seven Seas) is a supernatural action mystery. Detective Inugami comes to a rural village to look into a string of mysterious animal deaths and meets Kabane, a strange, quiet boy the villagers shun. Kabane turns out to be half kemono, a creature from Japanese folklore, and Inugami brings him to Tokyo to work at his detective agency. It's a fun mix of folklore, found family and monster action.
71: Radiant by Tony Valente (Viz Media) is a French-made fantasy adventure. Seth is a young sorcerer who lives in a world where monsters called Nemeses fall from the sky, and the few people who survive their touch gain magical powers. Determined to become a great Inquisitor hunter, Seth sets out to find the Radiant, the legendary source of the Nemeses, and destroy it. It's colorful, funny and energetic, great for fans of classic shonen.
73: Shaman King by Hiroyuki Takei (Viz Media) is a supernatural action adventure. Taking a shortcut through a graveyard, Manta Oyamada meets Yoh Asakura, a laid-back transfer student who can see and talk to ghosts. Yoh is a shaman training for the Shaman Fight, a tournament held every 500 years to choose the Shaman King, with the ghost of a legendary samurai, Amidamaru, as his partner. It's a fun classic with great battles and quirky characters.
74: Teasing Master Takagi-san by Soichiro Yamamoto (Yen Press) is a sweet middle school romantic comedy. Nishikata is constantly teased by Takagi-san, the girl who sits next to him, and he's determined to get her back just once. Every plan he makes falls apart, and he never seems to notice that she might like him. The short, gentle chapters make it a cozy read for anyone who enjoys light, wholesome romance.
75: Seraph of the End: Vampire Reign by Takaya Kagami (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy action series. After a mysterious virus kills everyone over the age of 13, the surviving children are taken captive by vampires, and Yuichiro Hyakuya escapes only at a terrible cost. Four years later, he joins the Japanese Imperial Demon Army, determined to take revenge. It's stylish and intense, for readers who enjoy dark action.
76: Days with My Stepsister by Yumika Kanade (Yen Press) is a quiet, slice-of-life romance. When Yuta Asamura's father remarries, Yuta suddenly gains a stepsister his own age, Saki Ayase, a girl from his school with a cool reputation. Having both seen their parents' marriages fall apart, they agree to keep a careful, honest distance, but over time their feelings slowly change. It's subtle and grounded, for fans of slow, realistic romance.
77: The Way of the Househusband by Kousuke Oono (Viz Media) is a deadpan comedy. Tatsu, known as "the Immortal Dragon," was once a legendary yakuza enforcer, but he's left that life behind to become a full-time househusband for his career-focused wife, Miku. He takes cooking, cleaning and grocery sales as seriously as he once took gang wars, and he still looks terrifying doing it. It's a funny, sweet read with short, easy chapters.
78: Call of the Night by Kotoyama (Viz Media) is a dreamy supernatural romance. Ko Yamori is a middle schooler who can't sleep and has quietly stopped going to school. Wandering the empty streets one night, he meets Nazuna Nanakusa, a playful girl who turns out to be a vampire, and learns that if he falls in love with her, he can become one too. It's moody, funny and atmospheric, perfect for night owls and fans of offbeat romance.
79: Samurai Deeper Kyo by Akimine Kamijyo (Tokyopop) is a samurai action adventure. Four years after the battle of Sekigahara, Kyoshiro is a gentle, goofy traveling medicine seller, but he shares his body with Demon Eyes Kyo, a feared swordsman. When bounty hunter Yuya Shiina sets out to collect the reward on Kyo's head, she ends up traveling with them. It's packed with sword fights and colorful rivals, great for fans of classic action manga.
80: Val x Love by Ryosuke Asakura (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy with plenty of action. Takuma Akutsu is a high schooler whose scary looks keep everyone away, so he has never had a single friend. Then the god Odin gives him a strange job: date the nine Valkyrie sisters, whose power grows with love, so they can fight off the monstrous Metals. It's a lively, fan-service-heavy harem story for readers who enjoy a big, colorful cast.
81: Moriarty the Patriot by Ryosuke Takeuchi and Hikaru Miyoshi (Viz Media) is a historical crime drama that tells the Sherlock Holmes story from the other side. In Victorian England, a rigid class system keeps the poor under the heel of the nobility. William James Moriarty, an orphan taken in by an aristocratic family, sets out with his brothers to tear that system down, one carefully planned crime at a time. It's a stylish, clever read for fans of mysteries and morally gray leads.
82: Sword of the Demon Hunter: Kijin Gentosho by Motoo Nakanishi (Seven Seas) is a quiet, melancholy historical fantasy. In the Edo period, the young swordsman Jinta serves as the guardian of the shrine maiden in Kadono, a remote iron-working village. When demons begin appearing near the village, he sets out to deal with them, and what he finds sets the course of a story that spans centuries. It's a thoughtful read for fans of samurai stories and Japanese folklore.
83: Murcielago by Yoshimurakana (Yen Press) is a violent, sexy crime action series for mature readers. Kuroko Koumori is a mass murderer who should have been executed long ago. Instead, the police keep her on as an assassin, sending her after the kind of killers no one else can stop, with a young driver named Hinako along for the ride. It's gory and over the top, and it knows exactly what it is.
84: Nana by Ai Yazawa (Viz Media) is a moving drama about friendship, love, and growing up. Two 20-year-old women, both named Nana, meet by chance on a train to Tokyo. Nana Komatsu is a romantic chasing after her boyfriend, while Nana Osaki is a punk singer determined to make it big with her band. When they end up sharing an apartment, their very different lives become tangled together. It's a grown-up story about the people who shape us.
86: Negima! Magister Negi Magi by Ken Akamatsu (Kodansha) is a magical comedy that grows into an action adventure. Negi Springfield is a 10-year-old wizard who has just graduated from magic school. His final training assignment is to teach English at Mahora Academy, an all-girls school in Japan, to a class of 31 students, all while keeping his magic a secret. It's a fun, busy series from the creator of Love Hina, with a huge cast to get attached to.
87: Fushigi Yûgi: The Mysterious Play by Yuu Watase (Viz Media) is a classic fantasy romance. Miaka Yuki is a junior high student cramming for her high school entrance exams. At the library, she and her best friend Yui find an old book called The Universe of the Four Gods, and Miaka is pulled inside. There, she is named the Priestess of Suzaku and must gather seven celestial warriors. It's a dramatic, heartfelt adventure for fans of '90s shojo.
89: By the Grace of the Gods by Roy (Square Enix) is a gentle, cozy fantasy. Ryoma Takebayashi was a worn-out office worker who died alone at 39. Three gods offer him a fresh start in another world, and he wakes up as a young boy in a quiet forest, where he spends his days taming and studying slimes. When he finally heads out into the world, his kindness and odd skills go a long way. It's a relaxing read for anyone who likes low-stakes isekai.
91: Akane-banashi by Yuki Suenaga and Takamasa Moue (Viz Media) is a drama about rakugo, the traditional Japanese art of comic storytelling. Akane Osaki idolized her father, a rakugo performer, until his dream of reaching the top rank ended in a single exam, when a powerful master expelled him and everyone else who took it. Years later, Akane steps onto the stage herself, determined to prove her father's rakugo was worth something. It's a warm, rousing story about craft, family, and finding your voice.
93: Magic Artisan Dahlia Wilts No More by Hisaya Amagishi (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy about making a life of your own. Dahlia Rossetti, an overworked employee in her past life in Japan, is reborn in another world as a maker of magical tools. On the day she and her fiancé are supposed to move into their new home, he calls off the engagement. Instead of wilting, Dahlia decides to live for herself and pour her energy into her craft. It's a gentle, satisfying read.
94: Record of Ragnarok by Shinya Umemura and Takumi Fukui, with art by Ajichika (Viz Media), is a fierce action series built around one-on-one battles. Every thousand years, the gods meet to decide humanity's fate, and this time they vote to wipe us out. The Valkyrie Brunhilde objects and proposes Ragnarok instead: thirteen duels between gods and history's greatest humans, with humanity's survival on the line. It's big, loud fun for fans of tournament fights and mythology.
97: The Abandoned Empress by Ina (Yen Press) is a romantic fantasy about getting a second chance. Aristia la Monique was raised from childhood to become empress and devoted herself to the crown prince. But when a mysterious girl appears from another world, Aristia is pushed aside, and her life ends in ruin. Then she wakes up as a ten-year-old again, with all her memories intact and a choice to make about who she wants to be. It's a thoughtful, emotional read.
98: The Tale of the Outcasts by Makoto Hoshino (Seven Seas) is a dark, gentle fantasy set in Victorian London, where monsters live hidden alongside people. Nell is a young orphan girl about to be sold off to a cruel life when she is rescued by Liam, a mysterious man who is far from human himself. The two set off together, and as they travel, an unlikely family begins to form. It's a moody, warm story for fans of found family and gothic folklore.
100: Horimiya by HERO and Daisuke Hagiwara (Yen Press) is a sweet, funny romance about the sides of ourselves we keep hidden. At school, Kyoko Hori is popular and put-together, but at home she's busy with chores and looking after her little brother. Her quiet, gloomy classmate Izumi Miyamura hides piercings and tattoos under his uniform. When they run into each other outside school, they discover each other's secret, and a friendship begins. It's a cozy, relatable read for romance fans.
103: Grand Blue Dreaming by Kenji Inoue and Kimitake Yoshioka (Kodansha) is a rowdy college comedy. Iori Kitahara moves to a seaside town to start university, living above his uncle's diving shop and dreaming of a fresh, sunny college life. Instead, he gets swept into the diving club, whose upperclassmen mostly seem to drink heavily and strip off their clothes. It's ridiculous, often crude, and very funny, with a real love of the ocean underneath.
104: Reign of the Seven Spellblades by Bokuto Uno and Sakae Esuno (Yen Press) is a dark school fantasy. Every spring, new students arrive at Kimberly Magic Academy, a prestigious school where danger is part of the curriculum and not every student makes it to graduation. Oliver Horn begins his first year there alongside a group of new friends, including Nanao Hibiya, a sword-wielding girl from a faraway land. It's a tense, rewarding read for fans of magic-school stories with real stakes.
105: Kakegurui: Compulsive Gambler by Homura Kawamoto and Toru Naomura (Yen Press) is a stylish psychological thriller. At Hyakkaou Private Academy, the children of the rich and powerful rank each other by gambling, and the losers become the school's pets. Then transfer student Yumeko Jabami arrives. She seems sweet and polite, but she doesn't gamble to win. She gambles for the thrill of the risk itself. It's tense, twisted, and dramatic, for readers who love mind games.
106: D.Gray-man by Katsura Hoshino (Viz Media) is a dark, gothic action fantasy. In an alternate 19th century, the Millennium Earl turns human grief into demonic weapons called Akuma. Allen Walker is a young Exorcist with a cursed left eye and an arm that can destroy them. When he arrives at the Black Order to join their fight, he steps into a much larger war. It's a moody, stylish series for fans of supernatural battles and memorable characters.
107: Edens Zero by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a bright, fast-paced space adventure. Shiki Granbell grew up on a planet-sized amusement park where the only other residents were robots. When Rebecca, a young video creator, and her blue cat Happy land there, Shiki leaves home for the first time and sets off with them across the cosmos. It's a fun, big-hearted series from the creator of Fairy Tail, full of friendship and wild new worlds.
108: Marmalade Boy by Wataru Yoshizumi (Seven Seas) is a classic shojo romantic comedy. High schooler Miki Koishikawa gets the shock of her life when her parents announce they're divorcing and swapping partners with another couple they met on vacation. Then all six of them move in together, including that couple's son, Yu Matsuura, who is good-looking and maddeningly hard to read. It's a breezy, funny '90s romance with real heart.
109: The Water Dragon's Bride by Rei Toma (Viz Media) is a fairy-tale fantasy romance. Asahi is a little girl living a happy, modern life until she falls into the pond in her garden and wakes up in another world. There, the villagers offer her as a sacrifice to the Water Dragon God, a powerful being who knows nothing of human feelings. It's a gentle, bittersweet story for readers who like slow-building romance with a mythic feel.
110: Shadows House by Somato (Yen Press) is a gothic mystery with a gentle, eerie charm. In a grand mansion live the Shadows, a family of faceless nobles covered in soot. Each one is served by a Living Doll who acts as their face. Emilico is a cheerful new doll assigned to a young Shadow named Kate, and as the two grow close, the house's strange rules start to raise questions. It's a beautifully drawn series for fans of puzzles and quiet unease.
113: Gachiakuta by Kei Urana (Kodansha) is a gritty, stylish action fantasy. Rudo lives in the slums of a city where the poor are looked down on and trash is thrown into the Pit, a place everyone believes means certain death. When Rudo is framed for murdering his foster father, he is thrown into the Pit himself. Surviving the fall, he lands in a wasteland full of trash monsters and vows to get back at the people who threw him away. It's raw and energetic, for fans of underdog heroes.
114: Cardcaptor Sakura: Master of the Clow by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a sweet magical-girl fantasy and the second half of the Cardcaptor Sakura story. Sakura Kinomoto has caught every Clow Card she accidentally set loose, but her work as a Cardcaptor isn't over. With her guardian Kero, her best friend Tomoyo, and her rival Syaoran, she faces a new and mysterious magic stirring in her town. It's a charming, gentle read for fans of the original series.
115: Skeleton Knight in Another World by Ennki Hakari (Seven Seas) is a lighthearted fantasy adventure. A gamer falls asleep playing his favorite online game and wakes up in its world, inside his character's body: a towering knight in legendary armor who is nothing but a skeleton underneath. Calling himself Arc, he hides his true form and sets out hoping for a quiet life as a mercenary. He doesn't get one. It's an easygoing read for fans of overpowered isekai heroes.
116: D.N.Angel by Yukiru Sugisaki (Tokyopop) is a fun, romantic supernatural adventure. On his fourteenth birthday, Daisuke Niwa works up the nerve to confess to his crush, Risa Harada. But the Niwa family carries a strange inheritance, and whenever Daisuke's heart races over her, he turns into Dark, a legendary phantom thief. Now he has to steal magical artworks while keeping his double life a secret. It's a charming 2000s shojo series with a dash of mystery.
117: Origin by Boichi (Kodansha) is a sleek sci-fi action series. In Tokyo in 2048, an android named Origin lives quietly among humans, passing as one of them. When other robots hidden in the city begin to put people in danger, he steps in to stop them, guided by the rules his creator left him. It pairs dazzling, detailed art with tight action, for fans of cyberpunk and robots.
118: My Neighbor Seki by Takuma Morishige (Vertical) is a quiet, clever comedy. Rumi Yokoi just wants to pay attention in class. Unfortunately, she sits next to Seki, who spends every lesson building elaborate games and tiny worlds on top of his desk, from domino runs to full chess battles. Rumi keeps trying to ignore him and keeps getting sucked in instead. It's a gentle, very funny read that's easy to dip in and out of.
119: A School Frozen in Time by Mizuki Tsujimura and Naoshi Arakawa (Vertical) is a chilling psychological mystery. On a snowy winter morning, eight high school students arrive at school to find it empty, the doors locked and the clocks stopped. Trapped inside, they slowly realize that a classmate who died by suicide at the school festival is somehow among them, but none of them can remember who it was. It's a tense, emotional story about guilt, friendship, and what we choose to see.
120: Ayakashi Triangle by Kentaro Yabuki (Seven Seas) is a supernatural romantic comedy with plenty of fan service. Matsuri Kazamaki is a young ninja sworn to protect his childhood friend Suzu, whose rare gift draws spirits called ayakashi to her. When Matsuri crosses Shirogane, the king of the ayakashi, the spirit gets revenge by turning him into a girl. Now he has to protect Suzu and sort out his feelings for her in a whole new body. It's goofy and sweet, for fans of ecchi comedy.
121: Fullmetal Alchemist by Hiromu Arakawa (Viz Media) is a gripping fantasy adventure. Brothers Edward and Alphonse Elric try to use alchemy to bring their late mother back to life, breaking its greatest taboo. The attempt goes horribly wrong: Edward loses an arm and a leg, and Alphonse loses his whole body, his soul bound to a suit of armor. Now the brothers search for the Philosopher's Stone, hoping to set things right. It's a beloved story about family, sacrifice, and doing the right thing.
122: Chio's School Road by Tadataka Kawasaki (Yen Press) is a silly, low-key comedy. Chio is an ordinary high school girl who'd rather be home playing video games. Every morning she has the same walk to school, and every morning it somehow turns into an adventure, whether she's dodging a classmate, climbing a wall, or imagining herself as the hero of her favorite shooter. It's goofy, offbeat fun for anyone who's ever made a game out of their commute.
123: Kowloon Generic Romance by Jun Mayuzuki (Yen Press) is a dreamy, mysterious romance. In the crowded, nostalgic streets of Kowloon Walled City, Reiko Kujirai works at a real estate agency alongside her teasing coworker, Hajime Kudou. As she falls for him, she learns that he was once engaged to a woman who looked exactly like her, and she starts to wonder how much she really knows about herself and the city. It's a moody, slow-burning story from the creator of After the Rain.
124: The Legend of Dororo and Hyakkimaru by Satoshi Shiki (Seven Seas), based on Osamu Tezuka's classic Dororo, is a dark historical action series. In war-torn Japan, a lord makes a pact with demons, promising them his newborn son's body in exchange for power. The baby, Hyakkimaru, survives anyway and grows up to hunt the demons one by one to take back what was stolen. Along the way, he's joined by Dororo, a scrappy young thief. It's a fresh, grim take on a classic.
125: Daughter of the Emperor by Yunsul (Yen Press) is a sweet fantasy comedy about winning over the scariest dad in the empire. A young woman is reborn as Ariadna, the newborn daughter of Emperor Ruveliss, a cold tyrant who killed his own family to take the throne. Remembering her past life and knowing just how dangerous he is, baby Ria sets out to charm her father before he decides she's expendable. It's adorable and funny, for fans of reincarnation stories.
126: Blood on the Tracks by Shuzo Oshimi (Vertical) is an unsettling psychological thriller about a mother and son. Seiichi Osabe is a quiet middle schooler living an ordinary life with his doting mother, Seiko, whose attention others call overprotective. Then, on a family hike in the mountains, something happens that shatters everything Seiichi thought he knew about her. It's slow, haunting, and hard to look away from, best for readers who like quiet horror and deep character study.
127: Mobile Suit Gundam Thunderbolt by Yasuo Ohtagaki (Viz Media) is a gritty, grown-up war story set in the Gundam universe. During the One Year War, the Thunderbolt Sector is a deadly stretch of space filled with wreckage and lightning. Federation pilot Io Fleming, a jazz-loving ace, and Zeon sniper Daryl Lorenz, a soldier who lost his legs in the war, find themselves on opposite sides of the fight there. It's tense, dramatic sci-fi for mecha fans and newcomers alike.
128: I'm in Love with the Villainess by Inori (Seven Seas) is a funny, heartfelt yuri romance. Rei Oohashi is an overworked office worker whose favorite thing in the world is a dating sim. When she wakes up as the game's commoner heroine, she has zero interest in the princes. She wants the haughty noble villainess, Claire François, and she isn't shy about saying so. It's a playful series that also has a lot to say about class and prejudice.
129: Taboo Tattoo by Shinjirou (Yen Press) is a fast-paced supernatural action series. Seigi Akatsuki is a high schooler with a strong sense of justice. After he helps a strange old man, he's given a mysterious tattoo, and it turns out to be a Taboo Tattoo, a secret weapon that grants incredible powers. Soon he's caught up in a hidden war between nations fighting over them. It's flashy, fun action for fans of martial arts and superpowers.
131: Prince Freya by Keiko Ishihara (Viz Media) is a sweeping fantasy drama. Freya is a quiet village girl who happens to look exactly like the kingdom's Prince Aaron. When the prince dies and their homeland is threatened by invasion, his knights ask Freya to take his place. To protect her people, she agrees to pose as the prince and lead them through a war. It's a moving story about courage, for readers who love royal intrigue and loyal knights.
132: The Summer Hikaru Died by Mokumokuren (Yen Press) is a quiet, creeping horror story. In a small rural village, Yoshiki and Hikaru have been best friends all their lives. But Hikaru went missing in the mountains for a week, and Yoshiki knows the boy who came back is not really him. Even so, he can't bring himself to let this new Hikaru go. It's eerie, tender, and deeply unsettling, for fans of slow-burn horror and complicated friendships.
133: Solo Leveling by Chugong and DUBU (Yen Press) is a fast, stylish action fantasy. When gates to monster-filled dungeons opened across the world, some people gained powers and became hunters. Sung Jinwoo is the weakest of them all, barely scraping by. After a raid gone wrong nearly kills him, he finds himself with a strange system only he can see, one that lets him grow stronger. It's a slick, satisfying power-up story with sharp, dynamic art.
135: Nisekoi: False Love by Naoshi Komi (Viz Media) is a lively romantic comedy. Raku Ichijo is the son of a yakuza boss, though all he wants is a normal life. To keep his family's gang from going to war with a rival gang, he has to pretend to date the rival boss's daughter, Chitoge Kirisaki, a girl he can't stand. Meanwhile, he's still holding onto a locket from a childhood promise. It's a sweet, silly love-triangle story for romcom fans.
136: Undead Unluck by Yoshifumi Tozuka (Viz Media) is a wild, inventive action comedy. Fuuko Izumo has a curse: anyone who touches her skin is struck by terrible misfortune. She's ready to give up on life when she meets Andy, an undead man who can't be killed and badly wants to find a death that sticks. Together, they make an unlikely team and stumble into a secret world of people with strange powers. It's fast and funny, with plenty of clever twists.
139: Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid by coolkyousinnjya (Seven Seas) is a sweet, silly comedy about a very unusual roommate. Kobayashi is a hardworking programmer who, after one drunken night in the mountains, invites a dragon to come live with her. To her surprise, the dragon, Tohru, shows up at her door the next morning in human form, ready to work as her maid. More dragons soon follow. It's cozy, funny, and full of heart, for anyone who enjoys found family.
140: Demon Slayer: Kimetsu no Yaiba by Koyoharu Gotouge (Viz Media) is an action fantasy set in Taisho-era Japan. Tanjiro Kamado is a kind boy who sells charcoal to support his family. One day he returns home to find them killed by a demon, and his younger sister Nezuko is the only survivor, now turned into a demon herself. Tanjiro sets out to become a demon slayer and find a way to make her human again. It's heartfelt and exciting, for fans of sword fights and family bonds.
141: Kase-san and Yamada by Hiromi Takashima (Seven Seas) is a gentle yuri romance. Yamada is a shy girl who looks after the flowers at her high school. Kase-san is the cool, athletic star of the track team. When the two start talking in the school garden, a sweet and slightly awkward romance begins, and the series follows them through the small, everyday moments of first love. It's soft and tender, a good fit for readers who want a low-drama love story.
142: Jing: King of Bandits: Twilight Tales by Yuichi Kumakura (Tokyopop) is a whimsical fantasy adventure and the follow-up to Jing: King of Bandits. Jing is a young thief with a legendary reputation, and his partner Kir is a wisecracking albatross with an eye for the ladies. Together they travel through strange, dreamlike cities in search of the world's most fabulous treasures, and most stories stand on their own. It's stylish, playful, and full of imagination.
143: Dai Dark by Q Hayashida (Seven Seas) is a strange, grimy, and darkly funny space adventure. Zaha Sanko is a boy with a big problem: his bones are said to grant any wish, so people all over the galaxy are out to take them. Instead of running, Zaha and his tough-talking living backpack, Avakian, decide to track down whoever is behind it all. It's wild and gory, from the creator of Dorohedoro.
146: Tsubasa: Reservoir Chronicle by CLAMP (Del Rey) is a fantasy adventure that hops between worlds. In the kingdom of Clow, the young archaeologist Syaoran is devoted to his childhood friend, Princess Sakura. When Sakura's memories scatter across other dimensions as magical feathers, her life is at risk. To save her, Syaoran teams up with the ninja Kurogane, the wizard Fai, and the creature Mokona to travel from world to world collecting them. It's packed with familiar faces from other CLAMP series.
147: Shy by Miki Bukimi (Yen Press) is a heartfelt superhero action series. In a world where peace is kept by heroes, one from each country, Japan's hero is Shy, a girl named Teru Momijiyama who is painfully shy. She can barely talk to people, even the ones she saves. But when a new threat appears, she'll have to find the courage to truly reach out to others. It's a sweet, earnest story about courage and connection.
148: Nichijou: My Ordinary Life by Keiichi Arawi (Vertical) is an absurd, everyday comedy. On the surface, life in this town is perfectly normal. Yuko, Mio, and Mai are three high school friends, and Nano is a robot girl who desperately wants to seem human, even with a giant windup key in her back. But the smallest moment can turn into total chaos. It's offbeat, surreal, and laugh-out-loud funny, best enjoyed one short chapter at a time.
151: To Your Eternity by Yoshitoki Oima (Kodansha) is a moving fantasy drama about what it means to be alive. An orb is sent to Earth with the power to take the shape of anything that leaves an impression on it. It becomes a rock, then a wolf, and then a lonely boy waiting for his people to return. As it wanders, it slowly learns to feel, to grow, and to lose. It's a beautiful, emotional story from the creator of A Silent Voice.
153: Given by Natsuki Kizu (Sublime) is a heartfelt boys' love romance about music. Ritsuka Uenoyama is a talented high school guitarist who has started to lose interest in playing. Then he finds Mafuyu Sato, a quiet classmate, clutching a broken guitar, and offers to fix it. When Ritsuka hears Mafuyu sing, it rekindles something in him, and soon Mafuyu joins his band. It's a tender story about grief, healing, and first love.
154: Ragna Crimson by Daiki Kobayashi (Square Enix) is a dark, intense action fantasy. In a world where dragons rule the skies, humans hunt them for a living. Ragna is one of the weakest hunters around, while his partner, Leonica, is a prodigy. When a powerful, scheming stranger named Crimson offers to help Ragna become strong enough to kill the dragon kings, Ragna takes the deal. It's brutal and dramatic, with huge, detailed battles, for fans of high-stakes fantasy action.
155: Alice in Borderland by Haro Aso (Viz Media) is a tense survival thriller. Ryohei Arisu is a bored high schooler who spends most of his time playing video games. One night, he and his two best friends find themselves in a version of Tokyo that's suddenly empty. To stay alive, they have to win deadly games, earning visas that buy them a few more days. It's gripping and brutal, for fans of puzzles and survival stories.
159: The Eminence in Shadow by Daisuke Aizawa (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy that pokes fun at isekai power fantasies. Cid Kagenou has one dream: to be the mysterious mastermind who secretly pulls the strings from the shadows. Reborn in a world of magic, he founds Shadow Garden, a secret organization dedicated to fighting a cult he made up. The trouble is, the cult turns out to be real, and his followers take him very seriously. It's a fun send-up for genre fans.
